projects.title: Hug Chair
projects.description:
From 13 April to 13 October 2025, representatives from countries across the globe gathered to showcase innovation, culture, and sustainability at the World Expo in Osaka, Japan. For Switzerland’s pavilion, MA Product Design students at ECAL were tasked with designing a stackable wooden chair to be produced in Japan by Karimoku New Standard, intended to furnish the light-weight, bubble-inspired architecture by Manuel Herz.

HUG is a circular chair that stacks inversely a feature that not only informs its name but also visually embodies the essence of collaboration. This versatile design accommodates a range of uses, from conferences to general pavilion seating.

projects.title: JK2 Synthesizer
projects.description: As a longtime synth-nerd and lover of all things music related, I’ve always dreamed of designing and building my own analog synthesizer. The journey began with defining the sound I wanted to create. Drawing inspiration from 1970s Minimoog schematics, I added a few modern touches to make it my own. From there, I designed and ordered custom PCBs, hand-soldered over 1200 components, and built a case focused for domestic spaces; combining aluminum and beech wood, I aimed for a synth that’s both easily transportable and visually balanced. Rugged yet refined.

projects.title: Lasso
projects.description: Lasso is a research project focused on repurposing discarded nylon climbing rope once it is deemed unsafe. Driven by an interest in high-performance materials, this exploration transforms soft rope into a rigid structure. By applying heat at 240–260°C, the fibers fuse together, creating a hardened plastic that can be shaped into furniture. From this principle, a series of 3 stools were created to showcase the potential of this technique.

about.text:
Jacob Kouthoofd Mårtensson is an industrial designer exploring how small, creative solutions can spark meaningful impact. With a background in Art Direction and a Master’s in Product Design from [ECAL](https://ecal.ch), this intersection allows him to craft iconic silhouettes, iterate quickly, communicate ideas clearly, and embrace the creative freedom to abandon what doesn’t work.

He has contributed to projects with studios such as Form Us With Love, Pentagram London, and SIMMER, for clients including Volvo, H&M, IKEA, and Disney.
